advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify the rc=1 on an mcp-only failure (after a successful bot deploy in the same tick) is not misinterpreted by systemd/alarming as a review-bot deploy failure.
evidence: line 685: `echo "$TARGET" > "$BOT_SHA_FILE.tmp" && mv ... ` (bot marker written before mcp block)
mcp fatal paths e.g. line ~741 `record_mcp_backoff_failure; exit 1`
ABSENCE: no test asserts the process rc on a tick where the bot deployed and mcp then failed (test_a_failed_mcp_deploy_does_not_redeploy_the_bot_every_tick checks command emission, not rc)
advisory.finding: The mcp fatal-failure paths still call `exit 1` (process-level) inside the inline mcp block, so on a tick where the review-bot deployed successfully (bot idle) and mcp then fails, the tick exits with rc=1 before the footer. bot-deployed-sha was already stamped at line 685 so the bot is not redeployed (the intended fix), but the global deployed-sha is left stale AND rc=1 is emitted for a tick in which the bot half succeeded — the exit code now conflates a bot-and-mcp complete deploy failure with an mcp-only failure. Confirm downstream alarming/monitoring on the service exit code does not treat this rc=1 as a full-deploy failure now that a bot success can coexist with it.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add/adjust a case where the bot is IDLE (in_flight=0, bot already at target) and the mcp backoff window is open, then assert a DOWNSTREAM step past the mcp block ran (e.g. the deployed-sha footer / observability marker) to prove the mcp skip did not stop the tick.
evidence: docstring: "While the mcp backoff window is open, mcp is SKIPPED — the tick itself continues." and "Scoping it to mcp means a failing mcp retries on a backoff schedule while every other path on the tick proceeds untouched."
setup: `_mcp_box_shared_change(mcp_box, in_flight=2)` — bot busy, so the tick defers

autodeploy.sh guard: `if [ "$bot_deferred" = 1 ] || [ "$bot_incomplete" = 1 ] || [ "$mcp_incomplete" = 1 ]; then exit 0` — a deferred bot stops the tick before observability/footer, so the test's absence assertions cannot distinguish 'mcp skipped, tick continued' from 'tick stopped at the bot deferral'
advisory.finding: test_mcp_backoff_window_skips_the_mcp_deploy_without_stopping_the_tick runs tick 2 with the bot busy (in_flight=2), so the tick exits at the bot_deferred guard `if [ "$bot_deferred" = 1 ] ...; then exit 0` regardless of mcp behaviour. The test therefore never verifies its stated distinguishing contract — that an mcp backoff SKIP lets the rest of the tick CONTINUE (reach observability/certbot/footer) rather than stopping the script. A mutation that made the mcp backoff branch `exit 0` (turning throttle-one-component back into stop-everything) would not turn this test red, because the tick already exits at the bot deferral.
advisory.suggested_fix: Run the mcp-backoff-skip tick with in_flight=0 and the bot already at $TARGET (BOT_SHA_FILE=$TARGET), then assert a post-mcp-block side effect occurred (deployed-sha advanced or the observability/certbot marker emitted), so the 'tick continues' contract is exercised rather than short-circuited by the bot deferral.

blocking.finding: bugfix-size-attestation: this change touches 163 non-test line(s) — over the 150-line floor for a bug fix — but bug cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95 has no acceptable plan-review attestation (verdict: unsigned; no plan-review attestation record). A fix like this is a design change wearing a bug label: write the fix plan into the ticket's description, run `rebar review-plan cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95` (it auto-escalates a bug with non-test file impact to the full review and SIGNS an attestation on a PASS; if the review passed but no attestation landed, `rebar sign-review cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95` re-persists it cheaply, and `rebar review-plan cf34-9b8b-1aa7-4d95 --status` confirms it is current without an LLM call), then re-push.
